title: Throughput Guardrails and TPS Regression Detector for Core Models
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a durable microbenchmarking and regression-detection suite that continuously measures tokens-per-second (TPS) and p95 tail latency for our core serving models. The suite should generate stable, reproducible workloads, record baseline metrics per model+shape, detect regressions against stored baselines, and fail CI or open a regression incident when thresholds are violated.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible workload generator that can run both synthetic token streams and traffic-replay traces (server-side) against hosted and dedicated endpoints.
The harness emits TPS and p95 metrics per run and persists results to the benchmarking store with model, sequence length, batch size, GPU type tags.
Regression detection logic that compares the last N runs to the canonical baseline and raises flags when TPS drops >10% or p95 worsens >15% (configurable by model).
Integration with CI: a GitHub Actions job and a periodic cadence job in our fleet that can fail the pipeline and post a regression PR comment with a link to the failure diff and dashboard.
Dashboards and an alert flow: onboarding to runtime-perf dashboards, and alerts to #perf-slo when a high-confidence regression is detected.
Documentation for how to add new models and shapes to the suite and how to update baselines after validated performance changes.
implementation_notes: Leverage the lightweight TPS harness from ENG-8219 as a starting point but replace single-run noise sources with a controlled sampler that supports warmup, KV cache priming, and deterministically seeded token sequences.

Use the existing metrics ingestion endpoint and add a 'benchmarking' namespace; each run writes metrics and an artifact JSON with run metadata to S3 (path: s3://redwood-benchmarks/{{model}}/{{date}}/{{run_id}}).
Store canonical baselines in the Benchmarks service (keyed by model+shape+hardware) and expose an API to update baselines only via an approval flow documented in the PR template.

Regression detector implements both statistical test (paired t-test on repeated runs) and absolute delta checks; flags include "likely-regression" and "noise-suspect" with minimum run counts to reduce false positives.

CI integration: GitHub Action job `bench/tps` will run on infra-impacting PRs and compare results against the baseline branch; a separate nightly GitHub Action job runs a matrix of representative shapes across core models and posts a summary to the perf dashboard.
Add p95 collection using the same microbenchmark but ensure histograms are exported from the runtime with high-resolution buckets to avoid aggregation artifacts.
tasks: Design workload shapes (seq 64/128/512/2048, batch sizes 1/4/8, eager vs streaming) and publish to runtime-performance/bench-shapes.md
Implement controlled workload generator (replay + synthetic) with deterministic seed and KV priming
Extend metrics write path to include benchmarking namespace and run artifact S3 upload
Implement regression detector service and baseline store APIs
Add GitHub Actions jobs for PR-level and nightly benchmark runs
Create perf dashboards and alerting rules in Grafana/Alertmanager
Write onboarding doc for adding new models and baseline update playbook
